newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast targets domestic savings at 30 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast targets domestic savings at 30 pct/GDP.

text.p: Ivory Coast is targeting a domestic savings level of 30 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to mobilise sufficient resources for investment, Economy and Finance Minister Ngoran Niamien said on Friday.

Niamien told a press briefing on a series of planned open days to introduce the public to the financial sector that the aim was to boost investment levels in the West African nation, already the world's top cocoa producer, to 30 percent of GDP.
The current level of savings is 11.3 percent.
Investment in 1996 hit 14.2 percent, up from 7.8 in 1993 -- before the 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc used widely in French-speaking Africa.
"The government aims to make Ivory Coast a newly industrialised nation within a generation," Niamien said.
"The strategy for achieving this is developing a dynamic private sector whose investments will constitute the primary motor of growth."
Niamien cited the role played by national financial systems in mobilising and allocating domestic resources for investment in the vibrant Asian economies.

"Experience shows us that developing countries that succeed are those with high investment levels of around 30 percent of Gross Domestic Product," he said. Funding investment needs required "a savings levels of at least 30 percent of GDP".

The open days will be held at the main conference centre in the commercial capital Abidjan from March 17-19. Financial institutions including the West African central bank, the African Development Bank and the World Bank will take part.
